resourceHint.vm: Servers you manage yourself (AWS EC2 · Azure VM · GCP Compute Engine, etc.)
resourceHint.block: Disks attached to servers for the OS and data (EBS · Managed Disk · Persistent Disk, etc.)
resourceHint.object: Storage for files, images and backups served by URL (S3 · Blob Storage · Cloud Storage, etc.)
resourceHint.egress: Data sent from your servers to the internet (inbound is mostly free). e.g. 1MB page × 1M views/month ≈ 1,000GB
resourceHint.k8s: Managed service that runs containers across servers (nodes) (EKS · AKS · GKE, etc.) — cluster fee + node servers
resourceHint.lb: Spreads incoming HTTP requests across servers (ALB · Application Gateway, etc.)
resourceHint.nat: Gateway for servers without public IPs to reach the internet (updates, external APIs) — needed when servers sit in a private network
resourceHint.db: MySQL/PostgreSQL with backups, patching and failover handled for you (RDS · Cloud SQL, etc.)
resourceHint.cache: Redis-compatible in-memory store for hot data — sessions, rankings, caching in front of the DB
resourceHint.container: Run containers always-on without managing servers (Fargate · Container Apps · Cloud Run, etc.)
resourceHint.cdn: Delivers static files like images and JS from locations near users (CloudFront · Front Door · Cloud CDN, etc.)
resourceHint.logs: Collects, searches and retains app/server logs (CloudWatch Logs · Log Analytics · Cloud Logging, etc.)

scenario.dbHaHint: Standby replica for high availability (AWS Multi-AZ · Azure HA · GCP Regional · OCI multi-node · NCP/SCP/NHN two servers · KT MySQL three nodes) — roughly doubles compute and storage (triples for OCI MySQL, which runs 3 instances)
scenario.cacheHaHint: High availability with a replica (AWS replica node · Azure two-node · GCP Standard tier · OCI/NCP/SCP/NHN replica node)
scenario.vmSkuLabel: Fill from the instance type you use (optional)
scenario.vmSkuNotFound: Not in this region's list — enter vCPU and RAM directly.
scenario.vmSkuPinned: {list} pinned · other platforms use the cheapest with at least this spec

estimate.noMatchArch: {provider} has no {arch} instances in this region — set Architecture to 'Both' to get an estimate
estimate.noMatchArchPlatform: {product} doesn't support {arch} — set Architecture to 'Both' to get an estimate
estimate.armNotice: ARM (Graviton · Ampere) instances require your app to be ARM (aarch64) compatible — you may need to recompile and verify dependencies.
estimate.sudNote: (sustained use discount not applied — up to {pct}% off automatically if run all month)
estimate.commitNotice: {years}-year commitment prices (no upfront) — AWS EC2 Instance Savings Plans and RDS/ElastiCache reservations, Azure reservations, GCP committed use discounts (CUDs), Samsung SCP Planned Compute (instance-type commitments), KT online VM commitments (VMs only, discount rate). OCI, NCP and NHN publish no per-resource commitments, so they stay at on-demand prices. Commitments apply only to VM, K8s node, DB, cache and container compute; storage, traffic, CDN, logs, load balancers, NAT and K8s control planes stay at on-demand prices. Committed charges are billed for the whole term whether or not you use them.
estimate.cheapestSummary: Cheapest — among {count} platforms offering every component
estimate.footnote: Linux on-demand list prices (or the selected commitment prices) × 730 hours/month. Per-account free allowances not included. The arrow (→) marks the cheapest instance that satisfies your specs, matched automatically. Storage compares general-purpose SSDs (gp3 · Premium SSD v2 · Balanced PD · OCI Balanced · NCP/SCP/NHN/KT SSD) and standard object tiers; traffic uses tiered internet-routing rates.
estimate.notOfferedRetention: {provider} keeps logs for at most {days} days
estimate.matchRule: → Auto-matched: the cheapest instance at or above your specs (vCPU·RAM; memory for caches) · {burst} · {arch}. You can change it from the dropdown.
